The third season of [[Invincible (TV series)|''Invincible'']], an American [[adult animated]] [[Superhero fiction|superhero]] television series created by [[Robert Kirkman]] who also wrote the comics. The season was produced by [[Amazon MGM Studios]] in association with [[Point Grey Pictures]], [[Skybound Entertainment#Subsidiaries|Skybound North]], Skybound Animation and Wind Sun Sky Entertainment, with Simon Racioppa serving as [[showrunner]]. In this season, [[Invincible (character)|Mark Grayson / Invincible]] ([[Steven Yeun]]) is forced to confront both his past and future as he grapples with the sacrifices necessary to protect his loved ones. Unlike the [[Invincible season 2|previous season]], this season does not include a mid-season break.

The season consists of eight episodes. The first three episodes were released simultaneously [[Amazon Prime Video]] on February 6, 2025, with the remaining episodes scheduled for weekly release until March 13, 2025.

As with previous seasons, the third season received critical acclaim for its acting, writing, storytelling, and character development. The season finale was also widely well received, with much of the praise going to the fight between Mark and Conquest.

 |ShortSummary    = Having witnessed his sister and niece's deaths during Mark and Nolan's fight in Chicago, GDA scientist Scott Duvall steals advanced bio-capacitors to augment his ability to convert kinetic energy into electrical power and publicly challenges Mark. Wishing to take the night off to celebrate William's birthday, Mark ignores Scott while Shapesmith answers his challenge. Scott defeats Shapesmith and flees to his wife Becky and son Jack, fearing GDA retaliation. As Robot works with Monster Girl to stop her powers from de-aging her body when she uses them, Rae confesses to Rex that she plans to retire from superhero work, which he accepts before they kiss. Amidst a memorial for the Chicago massacre, Scott takes the name "Powerplex" and tries to lure out Mark again, but is defeated and captured by Eve. Nonetheless, Scott escapes and returns to Becky, who suggests he stages her and Jack's kidnapping and use them as bait. Mark attempts to talk Scott down, but Scott accidentally kills his family while fighting Mark. After being taken into GDA custody, Scott vows revenge on Mark. Elsewhere, Angstrom gathers several of Mark's multiversal variants.

{{Episode list/sublist|Invincible season 3
 |EpisodeNumber   = 24

 |Title           = [[What Have I Done? (Invincible)|What Have I Done?]]
 |DirectedBy      = Haylee Herrick
 |WrittenBy       = [[Robert Kirkman]]
 |OriginalAirDate = {{Start date|2025|3|6}}
 |ShortSummary    = Angstrom sends his Invincible variants to destroy Earth and tarnish Mark's image. The GDA, the Guardians, and Earth's heroes are overwhelmed and suffer heavy losses. Scott briefly escapes; Eve is incapacitated; Rex sacrifices himself to save Robot, Monster Girl, and Bulletproof; Darkwing II is presumed dead; and the Immortal, Kate, Samson, and Shapesmith are wounded. When the surviving Invincibles turn on Angstrom, he traps them on a desolate Earth before battling Mark. Mark overpowers and nearly kills Angstrom, but he escapes to the Technicians, advanced cybernetic surgeons who previously healed him. Angstrom orders them to fix his wounds, but they refuse, demanding he repay them for all they have done for him. In the aftermath of Angstrom's attack, an aged Viltrumite envoy named [[Conquest (character)|Conquest]] arrives to survey Mark's subjugation of Earth for the Viltrum Empire and is disappointed by his lack of progress. Devastated by the destruction and deaths directed at him, Mark charges at Conquest to vent his rage.
 |LineColor       = E5E4E2

== Production ==
=== Development ===
''Invincible'' was renewed for a third season alongside [[Invincible season 2|Season 2]] on April 29, 2021, reflecting Amazon’s confidence in the series. [[Robert Kirkman]], the series creator, serves as co-showrunner with Simon Racioppa, with executive producers including [[Seth Rogen]], [[Evan Goldberg]], David Alpert, and [[Catherine Winder]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Petski |first=Denise |date=2021-04-29 |title='Invincible' Renewed For Seasons 2 & 3 By Amazon |url=https://deadline.com/2021/04/invincible-renewed-seasons-2-3-amazon-robert-kirkman-1234746788/ |access-date=2025-03-08 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Minton |first=Matt |date=2025-02-04 |title=Steven Yeun Teases 'Invincible' Season 3 as Creator Robert Kirkman Declares: 'I Don't Think Superhero Fatigue Is a Real Thing' |url=https://variety.com/2025/scene/news/steven-yeun-invincible-season-3-robert-kirkman-superhero-fatigue-1236297046/ |access-date=2025-03-08 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref> The season is produced by [[Skybound Entertainment]] and [[Amazon MGM Studios]], with animation handled by Wind Sun Sky Entertainment, Skybound North, and Maven Image Project. In May 2024, Ross Marquand stated that Season 3 was “nearly finished,” targeting an early 2025 release.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Echebiri |first=Makuochi |date=2024-06-18 |title=Did This 'Invincible' Star Just Reveal When Season 3 Will Come Out? |url=https://collider.com/invincible-season-3-release-window-ross-marquand/ |access-date=2025-03-08 |website=Collider |language=en}}</ref>

=== Animation ===
The season introduces Mark’s blue-and-black costume, teased in Season 2’s title card evolution, symbolizing his shift to a more hardened hero.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bove |first=Kate |date=2024-07-26 |title=Mark Grayson's Blue Suit In Invincible Season 3 Explained – Why He Wears It & What It Means |url=https://screenrant.com/invincible-season-3-blue-suit-mark-grayson-explained/ |access-date=2025-03-08 |website=ScreenRant |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mott |first=Sean |date=2025-02-28 |title=We Finally Know What Those 'Invincible' Title Cards Were Hinting at All Along |url=https://collider.com/invincible-season-3-title-cards-explained/ |access-date=2025-03-08 |website=Collider |language=en}}</ref> Animation quality has been enhanced, with Kirkman praising the work of the studios involved.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barnhardt |first=Adam |date=2023-10-15 |title=Invincible's Robert Kirkman Celebrates Artist Cory Walker's Contributions to the Animated Series |url=https://comicbook.com/tv-shows/news/invincible-robert-kirkman-praises-cory-walker-work-animated-series-prime-video/ |access-date=2025-03-08 |website=ComicBook.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Release ==
Season 3 premiered on February 6, 2025, with its first three episodes available on [[Amazon Prime Video]], followed by weekly releases every Thursday at 3:00 AM EST until March 13, 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Petski |first=Denise |date=2024-12-08 |title='Invincible' Season 3 Trailer: Mark Gets His Blue Supersuit In Preview For Prime Video Series — Update |url=https://deadline.com/2024/12/invincible-season-3-premiere-date-trailer-1236115859/ |access-date=2025-03-08 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Staff |first=Amazon |date=2024-12-20 |title='Invincible' Season 3 is now streaming on Prime Video—here's how to watch it |url=https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/entertainment/invincible-season-3-prime-video |access-date=2025-03-08 |website=www.aboutamazon.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rbHUhCcSXEM |title=Invincible Season 3 - Official Trailer {{!}} Prime Video |date=2024-12-07 |last=Prime Video |access-date=2025-03-08 |via=YouTube}}</ref> A teaser trailer was released in October 2024, featuring [[Invincible (character)|Mark]] and Cecil Stedman at Burger Mart, addressing the lack of a [[Hiatus (television)|mid-season break]] in response to [[Invincible season 2|Season 2]] criticism. A full trailer dropped in December 2024, showcasing Mark’s new training regimen and threats like the Mauler Twins and Reanimen.<ref>{{Cite web |author1=Jeff Spry |date=2025-01-27 |title='Invincible' Season 3: Release date, plot, and everything we know |url=https://www.space.com/entertainment/invincible-season-3-release-date-plot-and-everything-we-know |access-date=2025-03-08 |website=Space.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ashaari |first=Alleef |date=2025-02-06 |title=Invincible Season 3 Premiere Episodes Introduce New Suit & Status Quo In Mark's Life |url=https://www.kakuchopurei.com/2025/02/invincible-season-3-episodes-1-2-3-breakdown-easter-eggs/ |access-date=2025-03-08 |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Reception ==

=== Audience viewership ===
Audience reception was similarly positive. The season finale received a 9.9/10 rating on [[IMDb]], making it one of the highest-rated television episodes on the platform.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Aiello |first=Lauren |title=Review: ‘Invincible: Season 3’ packs a punch |url=https://fscollegian.com/2025/03/review-invincible-season-3-packs-a-punch/ |access-date=2026-06-13 |website=The Collegian}}</ref>

=== Critical response ===
The [[review aggregator]] website [[Rotten Tomatoes]] calculated a 100% approval rating based on 27 reviews were positive. The website's critics consensus reads, "Muddying the waters of justice and adding droplets of blood for good measure, Invincible and its titular hero reach their prime with this epic third season."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Invincible: Season 3 {{!}} Rotten Tomatoes |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/invincible/s03 |access-date=May 5, 2026 |website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |language=en}}</ref>

Timothy Lee of ''Geeks of Color'' praised the writing, character development, and action sequences, especially [[Conquest (character)|Conquest]]’s introduction and his battle with [[Invincible (character)|Mark Grayson]]. [[Steven Yeun]]’s performance was also praised. Lee noted that "Invincible shows that [[superhero]] stories can still be exciting if they put interesting characters, passion, creativity, and real stakes front and center," Lee, gave it 7 out of 10.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Color |first=Geeks of |title=‘Invincible’ Season 3 Has High Highs and Low Lows – Review |url=https://geeksofcolor.co/reviews/invincible-s3-review |access-date=2026-06-13 |website=geeksofcolor.co |language=en}}</ref> [[The A.V. Club|The AV Club]]'s William Hughes gave it a B, acknowledging that even with the fights lacking a particular distinctive punch, the season is still the stuff Invincible exists to dig into beneath all the arterial sprays and silly quips.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Walton Goggins saves the day, as usual, in Invincible's bloody season 3 premiere |url=https://www.avclub.com/invincible-season-3-premiere-recap-episode-1 |access-date=2026-06-13 |website=AV Club |language=en-US}}</ref>  Nate Richards of ''[[Collider (website)|Collider]]'' said the third season of Invincible is more drama-filled than the previous seasons, with much of the attention being paid to emotions and character interaction. Among the characters that received special attention in this season were Mark Grayson, [[Atom Eve]], Cecil Stedman, Rex Splode, and Oliver, as well as themes such as guilt, responsibility, and maturity. Additionally, many critics focused on the developing relationship between Mark and Eve, as well as the effects of previous events of the show on the characters' actions and decisions. Additionally, according to Richards, unlike previous seasons that featured an overall evil person, the third season lacks a specific antagonistic character in the form of [[Omni-Man]] or [[Angstrom Levy]], who would threaten the main characters in some way. Instead, Powerplex and Cecil act as conflicting forces for the [[Protagonist|protagonists]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Richard |first=Nate |date=2025-02-03 |title='Invincible' Season 3 Review: Prime Video's Superhero Series Still Packs a Mighty Punch |url=https://collider.com/invincible-season-3-review/ |access-date=2026-06-13 |website=Collider |language=en}}</ref>

=== Accolades ===
[[Steven Yeun]] received a nomination for [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Character Voice-Over Performance|Outstanding Character Voice-Over Performance]] at the [[77th Primetime Creative Arts Emmy Awards]] for his role as [[Invincible (character)|Invincible/Mark Grayson]] in the episode for "[[What Have I Done? (Invincible)|What Have I Done?]]."<ref>{{Cite web |title=19 total Invincibles in Season 3 and just 1 voice behind them all. The EMMY-NOMINATED @steveyeun!!! |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DMI1KhKvJ7u/?hl=en |access-date=July 15, 2025 |website=[[instagram]]}}</ref> Luke Asa Guidici, Matt Michael, Lea Carosella, and Liam Johnson received a nomination for [[Annie Award for Outstanding Achievement for Editorial in an Animated Television/Broadcast Production|Outstanding Achievement for Editorial in an Animated Television/Broadcast Production]] at the [[53rd Annie Awards]] for the episode "[[I Thought You'd Never Shut Up]]."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pedersen |first=Erik |date=2026-01-05 |title=Annie Awards: ‘KPop Demon Hunters’ & ‘Elio’ Lead Film Nominations |url=https://deadline.com/2026/01/annie-awards-nominations-2026-list-1236660651/ |access-date=2026-01-26 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref> Brad Meyer, Natalia Saavedra Brychcy, Katie Jackson, Noah Kowalski, Jayson Niner, Mia Perfetti, Logan Romjue, and Carol Ma were nominated for [[Golden Reel Award for Outstanding Achievement in Sound Editing – Sound Effects, Foley, Music, Dialogue and ADR for Non-Theatrical Animated Long Form Broadcast Media|Outstanding Achievement in Sound Editing - Non-Theatrical Animation]] at the [[Golden Reel Awards 2025]] for their work on the episode "I Thought You'd Never Shut Up."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pedersen |first=Erik |date=2026-01-12 |title=‘One Battle After Another’, ‘Sinners’ & ‘Stranger Things’ Lead MPSE’s Golden Reel Awards Nominations |url=https://deadline.com/2026/01/golden-reel-awards-nominations-2026-list-one-battle-stranger-things-1236680690/ |access-date=2026-02-08 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref>
